snip.t: Family history of renal disease: Inherited glomerulopathies (e.g., focal segmental glomerulosclerosis) are not uncommon.
Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS), glomeruli show lesions that are both focal (present only in a proportion of glomeruli) and segmental (localized to ≥ 1 intraglomerular tufts).
Example: In focal segmental glomerulosclerosis — only some glomeruli are affected (focal), and within those, only part of the tuft is sclerosed (segmental).

qs.q: What is the key microscopic finding that distinguishes Minimal Change Disease from Focal Segmental Glomerulosclerosis (FSGS)?
o: Deposition of IgG and C3 in the basement membrane
Presence of segmental sclerosis in glomeruli
Diffuse foot process effacement on electron microscopy
qs.e: The presence of glomerular sclerosis is the defining feature that distinguishes FSGS from MCD, which lacks sclerosis. Both conditions show diffuse foot process effacement on electron microscopy.

qs.q: A 45-year-old man with severe obesity develops progressive proteinuria and renal insufficiency over several years. What is the primary pathophysiological mechanism responsible for secondary focal segmental glomerulosclerosis in this patient?
o: Deposition of immune complexes within the mesangium
Glomerular hyperfiltration leading to podocyte stress
Complement-mediated injury to the peritubular capillaries
Direct antibody-mediated destruction of the basement
qs.e: In obesity, increased tubular reabsorption drives compensatory glomerular hyperfiltration, causing podocyte hypertrophy and subsequent sclerosis. Immune complex deposition is characteristic of IgA nephropathy or lupus nephritis rather than obesity-related FSGS.

qs.q: Which of the following is a first-line treatment for primary Focal Segmental Glomerulosclerosis (FSGS)?
qs.e: Corticosteroids are the first-line treatment for primary FSGS. Cyclosporine is a second-line agent, and ACE inhibitors are supportive measures for blood pressure control.

qs.q: What is the recommended second-line treatment for primary Focal Segmental Glomerulosclerosis?
qs.e: Calcineurin inhibitors like cyclosporine or tacrolimus are the second-line treatment for primary FSGS. Corticosteroids are first-line, and Rituximab is mentioned for Membranous Nephropathy.

qs.q: What is the prognosis for primary Focal Segmental Glomerulosclerosis (FSGS)?
o: Stable, without risk of renal insufficiency
Poor, many progress to ESRD within 5–10 years
Variable, depending on presence of hypertension
qs.e: Primary FSGS has a fair to poor prognosis and is generally resistant to steroids, with patients developing renal insufficiency within 5-10 years. MCD, in contrast, responds well to steroids.

qs.q: A research pathologist examines an electron micrograph of a glomerular lesion from an HIV-positive patient. The image shows large numbers of tubuloreticular inclusions within endothelial cells, alongside a collapsing variant of focal segmental glomerulosclerosis. What do these endothelial inclusions represent?
o: Modifications of endoplasmic reticulum induced by circulating interferon-alpha
Aggregates of immunoglobulin light chains typical of fibrillary pathology
Direct viral particles of human immunodeficiency virus within the cytoplasm
Deposition of circulating complement components from the alternative pathway
qs.e: Tubuloreticular inclusions within endothelial cells represent modifications of the endoplasmic reticulum induced by circulating interferon-alpha. They are also present in systemic lupus erythematosus and have diagnostic value on biopsy because they are absent in idiopathic FSGS.

qs.q: Which genetic variant is strongly linked to the high frequency of HIV-associated nephropathy and focal segmental glomerulosclerosis observed in Black patients?
qs.e: The racial disparity and high frequency of HIV-associated nephropathy in Black patients are primarily linked to G1/G2 risk alleles of the APOL1 gene. While NPHS2 mutations cause inherited forms of FSGS, they do not explain the specific ethnic predisposition to HIV-associated nephropathy.
qs.s: FSGS & HIV Nephropathy: Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis & Prognosis: MCQs

qs.q: What is the primary cellular target of injury in the pathogenesis of focal segmental glomerulosclerosis, classifying it fundamentally as a podocytopathy?
qs.e: Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis is considered a podocytopathy because the primary injury is directed at podocytes, leading to progressive podocyte loss and subsequent bare glomerular basement membrane sclerosis. While tubular cells and endothelium can be injured in specific variants like HIVAN, the core lesion stems from podocyte damage.
